text: Stability of the noise, not presence of it, decides gradeability; the repeat count is FLAT across every slide; and where a floor's structure is known it is a derived CEILING rather than a largest-observed value. MEASURED 2026-09-09, thirty captures of slide 14 by hash: THREE renders -- A=21 (0.700), B=8 (0.267), C=1 (0.033) -- so P(miss)=sum(p_i^n) is 56.2 percent at n=2, 16.9 at n=5, under 5 percent first at n=9 and under 1 percent at n=13. Thirteen captures per slide. AN ADAPTIVE PER-SLIDE COUNT IS REFUSED and this row said the opposite until it was measured: deciding a slide is stable requires the same evidence as proving it is, so escalating only the slides that look unstable under-detects exactly those that need it. THE TAIL IS CLOSED STRUCTURALLY, NOT SAMPLED: all three renders differ only at the two ENDPOINTS of one 59-pixel edge at x=145, so the renders are (top,bottom) with each end rounding independently -- A=(0,0), C=(0,1), B=(1,1), and a predicted D=(1,0). The maximum possible difference is both endpoints flipping, which IS A-to-B, so 0.002196 is a ceiling no unobserved mode can exceed. Confirmed independently by magnitude as well as geometry: RMSE(A,B)/RMSE(A,C) = 1.41404 against sqrt(2) = 1.41421, which is what 4 differing pixels against 2 of equal delta predicts.

state.evidence: SATISFIED on the 2026-09-09 run against artifact daaa503ad7db. FLAT COUNT: 13 captures a slide, every slide, plus one late-budget frame and one content-stripped control, no adaptive escalation. STABILITY IS A SEPARATE COLUMN from the floor that decides gradeability. THE CEILING IS TESTED RATHER THAN ARGUED, and this row was itself the prediction that tested it: two endpoints rounding INDEPENDENTLY predicts FOUR combinations, not the two it was written from. The run saw a THIRD render of slide 14 where ctl9 saw two, at exactly the distance independence requires -- one endpoint is 15 squared-difference units over rmse()'s divisor of 3*W*H and two are 30, so C-A and C-B are both sqrt(15/6220800) = 0.001553 and A-B is sqrt(30/6220800) = 0.002196, additive to the unit. That reproduces this row's independently measured RMSE(A,B)/RMSE(A,C) = 1.41404 from absolute counts rather than from a ratio. THE PREDICTIVE ARM ON SLIDE 13 IS STRUCTURAL AND NOT ARITHMETIC, which is snorkeltoast's correction to vc and it stands: the model, derived from a 59-pixel edge, predicts the SHAPE of slide 13's difference -- exactly four pixels, two per endpoint, at the two ends of a single vertical edge -- and counting on its 74-pixel edge confirmed it. vc had also offered sqrt(14/6220800) = 0.001500 against slide 13's reported floor as a second and stronger arm. IT IS NOT AN ARM AT ALL: rmse() IS sqrt(sum(d^2)/N), so that recomputes the reported figure from the same measured pixels and confirms the pixel COUNT rather than the model, which was never consulted on either side. Worth having as a consistency check that would catch a miscount; not evidence for the mechanism, and it is a correct number carrying more authority than it earned. THE CEILING IS NOW FALSIFIABLE AND THE UNUSED PREDICTIONS ARE ON THE RECORD IN FLOORS.md BEFORE ANY RUN TESTS THEM: slide 14's fourth state must land at 0.001553 or 0.002196; slide 13 has shown only two of four renders and a third must land at sqrt(7/6220800) = 0.001061 or at 0.001500. Any other distance falsifies the account, on slide 13 falsifying it on the slide the model was not built from. THE CEILING DOES NOT GENERALISE: any other multi-render slide is a lower bound until someone counts its pixels, because the mechanism must be identified before the argument is available at all. LIMIT ON THIS EVIDENCE, ADDED 2026-09-09 AFTER IT WAS FIRST WRITTEN: the artifact named by that sha is UNTRACKED -- 23 files, 15 MB, zero under git -- so the hash identifies the build and does not let anyone obtain it. The measurement happened and the numbers are real; what the sha cannot do is what a sha is for. AC-2.18 carries the property and the decomposition; this row is satisfied on its own terms, which concern the METHOD, and a reader should not take the sha as an offer of verification it cannot honour.
